I farm 18 mu here in Quzhou. Most of it — about 12 mu — I keep in the wheat-maize rotation like everyone in our village. That is the safe ground. Then I have 3 mu of cotton on the sandier piece by the road, and 3 mu of chili near the well because chili needs more water and I can watch it every day.

For wheat, I follow what I have done these past years. I put down a compound fertilizer 15-15-15 before sowing, about 50 jin per mu, then top-dress with urea around 30 jin at the green-up. That comes to about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu. The agro-input dealer in town keeps telling me I use too much, but my neighbor Old Wang cut back two years ago and his yield dropped — I am not taking that chance. I water four times: before winter, jointing, heading, and grain filling. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew, two times usually.

For maize after the wheat, I do not plough — direct seed with the machine, save time and money. The county station has been pushing this for years now and it works. I use a Zhengdan hybrid like most people. About 18 kg N per mu, mostly as base plus one top-dress. Water two times if the rains are poor. One spray for armyworm.

Cotton I plant as Bt hybrid — no choice these days, the bollworm would eat regular cotton alive. Cotton drinks potassium so I add muriate of potash. I plough this plot because cotton roots go deep. Five sprays at least — cotton is the most trouble.

Chili I treat as my cash crop. More fertilizer, more water, more spray. I aim for dried chili to sell. My daughter-in-law helps with the picking.

I am 69, my back is not what it was, and two of my sons work in the city. So I hire the combine and the seeder — only the management is mine.
